title: Glessner House's roof tiles checked against an 1887 photograph
items: Glessner House's Evidence panel now says what the earliest pictures show about its roof tiles. An 1887 photograph of the stable and a 1963 survey photograph count the same rows of tile up the same roof, about 42. So the 5-inch course the 1963 surveyors measured was already there when the house was new, and the roof keeps it. An earlier reading of about 6.4 inches came from that photograph's camera, not from the roof. The house itself looks the same.
